findings.title: order() mixin is off by one for legacy box layout
findings.body: The mixin emits the supplied value unchanged for both modern `order` and legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but the legacy properties are 1-based while `order` is 0-based (legacy default is 1, modern default is 0). Thus `order(2)` on .extra-info-wrapper and `order(3)` on .panel behave as ordinal-groups 2/3 in old WebKit/Firefox versus orders 2/3 in modern browsers, and any future `order(0)` would be invalid and `order(1)` would collide with unordered items in legacy browsers. The legacy declarations should use `$val + 1` so both models produce the same ordering.

findings.title: Flex conversion strands .small-action button next to the text instead of at the right edge
findings.body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex` (line 264), so its children become flex items and the `float: right` on its `button` (line 309) is ignored per the flexbox spec. Previously the float pinned the button (e.g. the dismiss/close control) to the right side of the row; now, with no `margin-left: auto`, `justify-content`, or explicit `order`/alignment on the button, it will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` on the left. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button (and drop the dead float) to preserve the right-aligned placement.

findings.title: align-items() omits the -moz-box alignment counterpart it claims to support
findings.body: `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for legacy Firefox, but `align-items()` provides no `-moz-box-align`, so the vertical alignment supplied here (e.g. `center` for `.d-header .contents` and `.small-action`, `baseline` for bullet badges) silently does not apply in the very legacy-Firefox layout mode the mixin set targets, leaving those rows top-aligned there. Also note `-ms-align-items` on line 121 is not a real IE10 property (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`), so it is dead code. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` (and remove/ignore the bogus -ms line) for consistent coverage.
